papers.title: Morse Neural Networks for Uncertainty Quantification
papers.abstract: We introduce a new deep generative model useful for uncertainty quantification: the Morse neural network, which generalizes the unnormalized Gaussian densities to have modes of high-dimensional submanifolds instead of just discrete points. Fitting the Morse neural network via a KL-divergence loss yields 1) a (unnormalized) generative density, 2) an OOD detector, 3) a calibration temperature, 4) a generative sampler, along with in the supervised case 5) a distance aware-classifier. The Morse network can be used on top of a pre-trained network to bring distance-aware calibration w.r.t the training data. Because of its versatility, the Morse neural networks unifies many techniques: e.g., the Entropic Out-of-Distribution Detector of (Macêdo et al., 2021) in OOD detection, the one class Deep Support Vector Description method of (Ruff et al., 2018) in anomaly detection, or the Contrastive One Class classifier in continuous learning (Sun et al., 2021). The Morse neural network has connections to support vector machines, kernel methods, and Morse theory in topology.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该论文提出了一种通用的不确定性量化深度生成模型，可迁移至代理模型的不确定性评估。
llm.why_not_core: No application to finite element or surrogate modeling; no constraint handling or optimization; no biomedical or implant context.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有不确定性量化方法难以处理高维子流形模式。
summary_zh.method: 提出Morse神经网络，推广未归一化高斯密度以表征子流形模式。
summary_zh.result: 该模型统一了多种技术，如OOD检测、异常检测和连续学习。
summary_zh.validation: 理论分析及与现有方法的联系。

summary_en.motivation: Current uncertainty quantification methods are limited to modeling modes as discrete points rather than high-dimensional submanifolds.
summary_en.method: The Morse neural network generalizes unnormalized Gaussian densities to represent modes as submanifolds, trained via KL-divergence minimization.
summary_en.result: The model provides a unified framework for out-of-distribution detection, anomaly detection, and calibration.
summary_en.validation: Theoretical connections to support vector machines, kernel methods, and Morse theory are established.

papers.title: Bounce: Reliable High-Dimensional Bayesian Optimization for Combinatorial and Mixed Spaces
papers.abstract: Impactful applications such as materials discovery, hardware design, neural architecture search, or portfolio optimization require optimizing high-dimensional black-box functions with mixed and combinatorial input spaces. While Bayesian optimization has recently made significant progress in solving such problems, an in-depth analysis reveals that the current state-of-the-art methods are not reliable. Their performances degrade substantially when the unknown optima of the function do not have a certain structure. To fill the need for a reliable algorithm for combinatorial and mixed spaces, this paper proposes Bounce that relies on a novel map of various variable types into nested embeddings of increasing dimensionality. Comprehensive experiments show that Bounce reliably achieves and often even improves upon state-of-the-art performance on a variety of high-dimensional problems.

llm.relevance_to_user: 该方法可用于生物力学设计中的混合变量优化，但缺乏实际应用案例。
llm.why_not_core: does not address FEA surrogates, constraint handling, or uncertainty quantification, and no application to implant/biomechanics design.

summary_zh.motivation: 现有贝叶斯优化方法在高维组合空间中不可靠。
summary_zh.method: 提出Bounce算法，利用嵌套嵌入映射不同变量类型。
summary_zh.result: 在多种高维问题上稳定达到或超越现有最优性能。
summary_zh.validation: 在标准基准问题上的综合实验验证。

summary_en.motivation: Existing Bayesian optimization methods for combinatorial and mixed spaces are unreliable, especially when the function optima lack certain structure.
summary_en.method: Bounce introduces a novel map of variable types into nested embeddings of increasing dimensionality to handle combinatorial and mixed spaces robustly.
summary_en.result: Comprehensive experiments demonstrate that Bounce reliably achieves or improves upon state-of-the-art performance on diverse high-dimensional problems.
summary_en.validation: Validation is performed on a variety of high-dimensional benchmark problems from combinatorial and mixed optimization.
